claims.text: Adding approximately 5 atomic percent copper to the high-entropy alloy will promote copper enrichment at grain boundaries.
Copper-enriched grain boundaries will form interconnected thermal pathways.
The interconnected copper-enriched pathways will enhance heat-transfer efficiency.
The copper addition will maintain structural robustness under plasma-facing conditions.
Approximately 5 atomic percent copper should be incorporated during alloy fabrication.
The proposed effect is expected to hold at temperatures of 600–800 °C under thermal cycling and mechanical stress loading.
Copper-enriched grain boundaries act as localized high-thermal-conductivity channels in the high-entropy-alloy matrix.
Copper has high electronic thermal conductivity.
Controlled grain-boundary segregation of copper will create interconnected networks that improve heat conduction.
Controlled copper segregation will not significantly compromise microstructural integrity or mechanical strength.
The copper-modified alloy will have roughly 15–20% higher thermal conductivity than current intermediate-layer material.
The copper-modified alloy will preserve mechanical strength and ductility under the stated operating conditions.
Undesirable copper-containing second phases could offset the heat-transfer benefit by causing embrittlement or loss of structural integrity.
The magnitude of the conductivity improvement and long-term stability under cyclic plasma and irradiation conditions are uncertain.
